blocks.text:
This was Alexandra's favorite park
in all of Grass Valley.
Alexandra ran in, ready to play.

Swings. Tunnels. Sand.
A climbing wall like a mountain.

Kids whooshed all the way
to the bottom.
It also looked very, very tall.

The slide looked even longer
from here.

Alexandra did not
know what to do.

That night,
Alexandra sat quietly
on the bed.

The big feeling
was still there.
"That was scary," said a tiny voice.

A light blinked
beside the bed.

The lights made a path
across the floor.

"Let's look together,"
said the tiny voice.

"This way,"
said the voice.
"Whenever you're ready."

On the quiet path
lay a clue:

Before Alexandra could peek,
voices called from every direction.

"This way!" blinked a star.
"No, this way!" puffed the wind.

"Hop!" said a mushroom.
"Skip!" said a stone.

"Too many voices make it
hard to hear your own,"

Alexandra listened for
the small, true voice inside.

And there it was:
a quiet path.

One way was smooth and shiny.
It looked easy.
The other was plain and steep.

Alexandra looked at the shiny path.
It was pretty.
At the top, a cave glittered.

Alexandra felt scared.
Alexandra's tummy felt tight.
The tiny voice echoed through the cave.

The same words glowed on it
in big, prickly letters.
The tiny voice didn't sound friendly now.

"Why do you sound mean?"
asked Alexandra.

The voice was quiet.
Alexandra remembered.

The words opened.
Inside were smaller words:
I'M A LITTLE SCARED.  THIS FEELS TOO BIG.
"Oh. You weren't trying to be mean."
The tiny voice felt warm again.

"Sometimes big feelings
come out sharp," said the voice.

"But if you listen close,
you can hear what they
are really trying to say."

The prickles fell away.
The wall shimmered.

Beyond it,
the world was bright.
Alexandra felt a little better now.
The tiny voice helped them notice

"I want to see you,"
said Alexandra.
A trail of feathers glowed ahead.
The forest grew warmer and quieter.

"Listen close," said the tiny voice.
"That quiet is your heart."

In a warm, magical clearing,
Owl appeared.

"I am your quiet voice," said Owl,
"in a shape you can see."

The warm quiet was inside
Alexandra, too.

Alexandra and Owl flew
through the stars.
The magical forest grew small below.

Ahead was the park, the ladder,
and the very, very tall slide.

Owl stayed close.
So did the quiet voice.
Alexandra was back at the top.

The slide still looked long.
The slide still looked fun.
The slide still looked very, very tall.

This time, Alexandra
knew what to do.

The quiet voice was there.
Small and warm.

Alexandra looked at the child
waiting behind them.
Trace the spiral with your finger.

Breathe in as you go around.
Breathe out as you come back.
Think of something you'd like to try.
How does it make you feel?

Listen close. Does your quiet voice say
"no," "not yet," or "yes"?

Ask your child: "Was there a time today
when you felt ready, or when you
wanted to wait?"
